reception: Among citing works VeGen figures chiefly as a marker in the vectorization literature: papers on tensor compilers and SIMD code generation list it among approaches that reach beyond packed SIMD, usually in a sentence or two. The substantive engagement comes from synthesis-based vectorizers and instruction-selection work — Coyote, vector instruction selection for digital signal processors using program synthesis, Minotaur, and Hydride — which position their techniques against VeGen's generation of a vectorizer from instruction semantics. The record is modest and skews toward brief mentions, but the works that do engage are those pursuing the same question of retargetable vector code generation. The implementation is available as ychen306/vegen, and the paper carries Artifacts Evaluated & Functional and Results Reproduced badges.
